correctness.rationale: Fourier-Plancherel gives the exact multiplier norm 2^k max y^(k/2)|r(y)|. Under z=(k/2)(1-y), fixed n Vandermonde bounds and normalization force monic limiting polynomials, while (1-z/K)^K<=e^(-z) gives uniform upper bounds and lower bounds at every fixed z. Polynomial-coefficient convergence yields the centered binomial kernel, and exponential tails force maximizers into an O(k^-1/2) Nyquist layer. The n=2 constant follows from three alternating extrema and unique scalar equations; the positive value follows by pointwise quadratic-square domination. The stored checker independently tests algebraic normalization, exact critical contacts, the positivity value, and finite-order convergence. No experiment is used as proof of an infinite limit.

value.rationale: The source leaves most higher derivative-order sharp smoothing problems open. This theorem resolves the entire high-derivative regime at every fixed finite support radius, gives the universal binomial limiting optimizer, exact Nyquist boundary-layer localization, and strictly quantifies the Fourier-positive penalty. The first five-tap free sharp constant is a nontrivial natural invariant with an exact transcendental two-contact reduction and numerical value, while the existing positivity constant lets it be compared on a common normalization. This is a structural answer across all radii and a concrete first new case, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
